title: Hold feedback until the linked answer
statement: When one answer leads straight into a linked one, hold feedback on the first until the second is given, because a verdict on the first can answer the second.
detail: On the opening question of a Grade 3 reading build's main conversation, the child says an answer and then taps the line that proves it, and once spoken answers were read by a marker, a note about what the child said appeared under the reply to the tap. The note is held until after the tap on purpose, because a reply that reacts to whether the spoken answer was right would answer the tap before the child makes it.
against: The same build's two-part evidence items settle the first part before the second: "Part B is hidden until Part A is answered correctly" (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/CONTENT-SCHEMA.md`, line 270), so a learner knows the first part's verdict before the second part appears.
